verifications.claim: President Donald Trump fired U.S. Attorney General Pam Bondi on April 2, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Trump fires Attorney General Pam Bondi (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/02/...)' ; R2: 'Trump fires Bondi as attorney general (https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/trump-fires-bondi-as-attorney-general)' ; R3: 'published at 20:39 BST 2 April' ; R4: 'President Trump fired Attorney General Pam Bondi on Thursday'
verifications.reasoning: All sources directly confirm Trump fired Bondi on or around April 2, 2026, matching URLs and publication dates.

verifications.claim: Pam Bondi's tenure as U.S. Attorney General lasted 14 months.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Bondi’s firing ends a turbulent 14-month term' ; R5: 'During her 14 months as attorney general'
verifications.reasoning: R4 and R5 explicitly state 14-month tenure; others approximate 'over the past year' consistently.

verifications.claim: Bondi faced pressure over the Department of Justice's handling of Epstein-related documents.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Epstein files fallout', 'bungled the release' ; R2: 'scrutiny over the Justice Department's handling of files related to Jeffrey Epstein' ; R3: 'frustration... over her handling of the Epstein files' ; R4: 'frustrations... over her handling of the Epstein files'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly describe pressure, frustration, and criticism over DOJ's Epstein files handling.

verifications.claim: Bondi failed to prevent the public release of sensitive, high-profile names in Epstein-related documents.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Sources criticize Bondi for delaying, withholding, or mishandling releases (e.g., not redacting victims), but none state she failed to prevent release of sensitive high-profile names; narrative is opposite (slow-walking releases).

verifications.claim: Trump was consistently frustrated that Bondi did not move quickly or effectively enough to investigate and indict his political enemies, such as Letitia James and James Comey.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Trump had pushed Bondi to criminally charge Comey and James' ; R2: 'struggled to satisfy Trump's demands to prosecute his political rivals... Comey and James' ; R3: 'delays in those cases were "killing our reputation"' ; R4: 'failed efforts to prosecute his political enemies... inability to secure indictments' ; R5: 'indicted... Comey... and Letitia James... thrown out'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly confirm Trump's frustration over slow/ineffective prosecutions of named enemies like James and Comey.

verifications.claim: Trump complained frequently to allies about Bondi's performance.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'President Trump had complained too freely, too frequently, to too many people about her inability' ; R1: 'Trump in recent days has been talking to Republicans and allies about removing Bondi' ; R4: 'privately venting his frustrations for months' ; R7: 'Trump had been frustrated with Bondi on multiple fronts, sources said'
verifications.reasoning: R6 directly states frequent complaints to many; others confirm discussions with allies.

verifications.claim: The decision to fire Bondi followed her failure to secure a graceful exit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'Pam Bondi Wanted a Graceful Exit. But Trump Wanted Her Gone.' ; 'hoped... to buy a little more time... to give herself a graceful exit. She ended up with neither'
verifications.reasoning: R6 explicitly describes Bondi's attempt and failure to secure graceful exit, leading to abrupt firing.

verifications.claim: Bondi's firing followed the removal of other cabinet members.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Her ouster comes weeks after Trump terminated another cabinet member, Kristi Noem' ; R3: 'comes just weeks after he removed Kristi Noem' ; R4: 'second cabinet member in recent weeks... ousted Kristi Noem' ; R5: 'second cabinet secretary... fired homeland security head Kristi Noem'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state Bondi's firing followed recent removal of Noem and note trend.

verifications.claim: Todd Blanche was named as the acting attorney general following Bondi's departure.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Deputy Attorney General... Todd Blanche, will step in to serve as Acting Attorney General' ; R3: 'deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche will step in... in an acting capacity' ; R4: 'replacing Ms. Bondi with Todd Blanche, her deputy, on an interim basis'
verifications.reasoning: All major sources confirm Blanche named acting AG post-Bondi.
